page: Google Cloud Platform x5-688-16t-metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized server configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 688 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16,384 GB of system memory, delivering an allocation ratio of 23.81 GB of RAM per core. The platform operates without integrated discrete GPUs and does not bundle local disk storage. Network connectivity operates without complimentary public IPv4 addresses included in the baseline provisioning.

With bare-metal execution and dedicated core assignment, the server avoids hypervisor overhead for extreme compute and memory footprint demands. The absence of attached local storage necessitates network-attached storage architectures for all non-volatile persistence. Similarly, the lack of onboard accelerators targets the platform entirely at CPU-driven operations requiring colossal memory structures rather than GPU-accelerated computing pipelines.

From a resource density perspective, this instance consolidates massive memory-to-core ratios onto a single bare-metal host, targeting enterprise setups requiring unified memory spaces without distributed scaling complexity. Workloads matching this hardware profile include massive in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise resource planning systems such as SAP HANA, real-time analytics over multi-terabyte datasets, and large memory-resident batch jobs.
